clue.text: Maybe Mark and Mike defending American hymns

parts.note: Mark's is one of the four Gospels, hence 'maybe'

indicators.note: to defend something is to stand around it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a mike is a microphone, short form mic

explanation.surface: Mark and Mike stand guard over the American hymns, like two choir members.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike is not the NATO letter M here but the microphone, MIC, which holds US.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel music is the genre of rousing Christian songs, especially from Black American churches, so hymns in a broad sense.

clue.text: Put request in to obtain seal

indicators.note: put ... in is an instruction to place one piece inside another

explanation.surface: Someone files a request to be given a seal, as for an official document.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is split: 'Put' and 'in' together tell you to place one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasket is a flat ring or sheet fitted between two surfaces of an engine or pipe to stop leaks.

clue.text: Singular beauty title for extraordinary torch-bearer

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their usual order

explanation.surface: A beauty queen wins a special title for carrying the torch, perhaps at a pageant.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant figure in New York Harbor holds a flaming torch aloft in her raised right hand.

clue.text: Cross middle of Sahara in transport emitting smoke?

indicators.note: in places the cross and the desert's centre inside the word for transport

parts.note: transport in the sense of rapture or delight
X is shaped like a cross

indicators.note: only the central letters of the desert's name are taken

parts.note: the two central letters of the six

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses the Sahara in a smoking vehicle, a camel train or old steam engine.
explanation.walkthrough: Transport is the feeling, not the vehicle: to be transported is to be carried away with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhalation is breathing out, and the question mark admits a smoker breathing out smoke is only one example.

clue.text: Hand first of these into US college

indicators.note: into places that letter inside the college's initials
only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand in some papers to an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: Inserted before the final T of MIT the result reads the same as tacking it on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mitt is slang for a hand, as in 'get your mitts off'.

clue.text: Part of patient's hip can allow artificial passage

indicators.note: only a stretch of the following words is wanted, running across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the fourth

explanation.surface: A hospital patient's hip replacement makes walking possible again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artificial passage' sounds medical in this hospital scene, but it is a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship canal is a man-made waterway deep enough for seagoing vessels, such as the Manchester Ship Canal.

clue.text: Roughly dodge over a gap in line

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means approximately

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a dodge is a trick or ruse

explanation.surface: A rough instruction to swerve across a gap in a queue or a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A caesura is a pause or break in the middle of a line of verse.

clue.text: Hardworking river threesome, plus you and I

parts.note: you and I together are us

explanation.surface: A diligent group of three people working along a river with the narrator.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrious describes someone who works steadily and diligently, the same sense as hardworking.

clue.text: Fuel is in jars with boron that's not easily melted

indicators.note: something that jars is shaken up, so these letters are jolted out of order

parts.note: B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: fuel kept in jars with boron becomes hard to melt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jars' looks like containers but works as a verb meaning shakes; 'with boron' adds its letter to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infusible cannot be fused, meaning it resists being liquefied by heat.

clue.text: Lawyer, showing embarrassment, took risk

parts.note: a district attorney in the US
the colour of an embarrassed face

explanation.surface: A blushing lawyer has taken a gamble in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare is to have the courage to do something risky, so dared is the past tense of venturing.

clue.text: Warmer second layer covering humble character

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
Uriah Heep, the 'umble clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield
a skin is a thin outer layer

explanation.surface: Advice on dressing warmly: add a second layer over a modest person.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply follow one another; 'covering' is loose, as the layer ends up after the character, not round him.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin coat or rug keeps you warm, so it is a warmer in the sense of something worn for heat.

clue.text: With roadie, joiner blended into city

indicators.note: things blended are mixed together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A band's roadie and a carpenter melt into the life of a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is the major Brazilian city famous for its carnival and Sugarloaf Mountain.

clue.text: Pariah has to expose actors

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them

explanation.surface: A shunned person is forced to reveal secrets about some actors.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone rejected by society, the same idea as a pariah.

clue.text: Sieve stones at bottom of mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone sifts the stones lying at the foot of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is a coarse riddle or mesh used to sort gravel and soil, so a kind of sieve.

clue.text: Get this in order to collect dad's food

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so the mixed letters hold the father
putting things in order means rearranging them, so these letters are sorted afresh

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad; the 's is ''s' as in has

explanation.surface: A child is told to tidy up so they can fetch their father's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order' sounds like 'so that', but it means rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin pasta, a staple Italian dish and so a kind of food.

clue.text: Exact helping of chicken for celebrity

indicators.note: a helping is a portion, so only a slice of the following words is served

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the third

explanation.surface: A celebrity is served a precise portion of chicken, perhaps on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact' reads as an adjective meaning precise; here it is the verb, pronounced with the stress on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact obedience or payment is to demand and compel it, which is to enforce it.

clue.text: Soldiers catch truck to reach target circle

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the soldiers' letters close around the vehicle

parts.note: a ute is a utility vehicle or pickup, chiefly Australian

explanation.surface: Troops jump on a lorry to get to the firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the standard crossword shorthand for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery or rifle target the outer is the outermost ring, scoring least, beyond the bull and inner.

clue.text: Matches for peers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the verb, is the same as
second meaning: people of the same standing

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns or verbs of other kinds: matches for lighting, peers who gaze or sit in the Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Equals as a verb means corresponds to exactly, and as a plural noun means those of equal rank or ability.

clue.text: Damnable Republican stopping person in dock

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the letter sits inside the defendant

parts.note: the defendant standing in the dock of a court

explanation.surface: A wicked politician interrupts a defendant's trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means under a curse or hateful, the same as damnable, deserving damnation.

clue.text: Herald newspapers cut time

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the word for newspapers loses its last letter

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A newspaper called the Herald cut its publishing hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Herald is a common newspaper name, which is why it looks like the subject; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to announce or foreshadow its coming, which is to presage it.

clue.text: Popular outcome? Pretty much

explanation.surface: A query about whether the result of something is going down well with the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes the two first words look like a query about a result being popular.
explanation.definitionFit: In effect means virtually or for all practical purposes, which is what pretty much means.

clue.text: Don't eat on holiday in Asia perhaps? Not even this?

definitions.text: Don't eat on holiday in Asia perhaps? Not even this?

indicators.note: on in an across answer means placed after, so the fasting comes behind the holiday

parts.note: a short holiday is a break
to fast is to go without food
Asia is an example of a continent

explanation.surface: A dieter on an Asian holiday is told not to eat, not even the hotel's bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the fasting after the holiday. The whole clue then defines the meal: a light hotel breakfast is so little that skipping it barely counts.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental breakfast is a light morning meal of coffee, rolls and pastries, the bare minimum a hotel serves.

clue.text: Victoria was one alluring woman, missing time and time again

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so letters for time are dropped from the woman

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, needed twice

explanation.surface: A historical note that Queen Victoria was a seductress, though perhaps lacking time for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ts of the seductress go, the first and the one in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria took the title Empress of India in 1876.

clue.text: Rank girl provided in case of custody

indicators.note: in puts the girl and the condition inside those outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: A girl is given a ranking provided she is kept in a custody case.
explanation.definitionFit: To rank things is to sort them into grades or order, which is to classify them.

clue.text: Twice ring very loudly to cancel

indicators.note: twice tells you to use the following word two times, each time in a different sense

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: Someone phones twice, very loudly, to cancel an appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' says use the word ring twice, in two different senses: the phone call and the round shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To call off an event is to cancel it, a common phrasal verb.

clue.text: Fish boxes offering spaces for wheels

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box, like the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's crates leave room for a cart's wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' is slang for a car, as in 'nice wheels'.
explanation.definitionFit: Car parks are areas where vehicles are left, so spaces for wheels in the slang sense of cars.

clue.text: Wreck large old exhaust

parts.note: to exhaust supplies is to use them up

explanation.surface: A big, ancient car exhaust pipe has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' tempts as the car part; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To louse up something is informal for spoiling or ruining it, which is to wreck it.

clue.text: Frankfurter maybe wanting Salvation Army employment

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the charity's initials are taken out

parts.note: a frankfurter is a kind of smoked sausage

explanation.surface: A man from Frankfurt seeks a job with the Salvation Army.
explanation.walkthrough: Frankfurter looks like a citizen of Frankfurt; the 'maybe' shows it is an example of the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage and employment both mean the act of using something, as in the employment of a tool.

clue.text: Required amount in syringe, ignoring foreign article

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so the article is dropped

parts.note: as much as a needle holds

explanation.surface: A nurse measures the dose required in a syringe, ignoring an imported item.
explanation.walkthrough: The LE comes from the middle of the needle's measure, not its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful means necessary, so something needful is required; 'the needful' is what must be done.

clue.text: Following Mrs Thatcher is a clumsy man with sack

indicators.note: something clumsy is awkwardly put together, so these letters are fumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cabinet minister succeeding Mrs Thatcher is a clumsy fellow who was sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a man given the sack; the sack is the one full of presents.

clue.text: Catch Yankee assassin

parts.note: a rub is a snag or catch, as in 'there's the rub'
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An order to seize an American killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ruby was the Dallas nightclub owner who shot Lee Harvey Oswald, President Kennedy's assassin, in 1963.

clue.text: Soldiers once trained actors, including journalist

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the mixed letters take in the journalist
trained suggests being drilled into new shape, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Former soldiers have trained as actors, with a reporter along for the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoats were British soldiers of past centuries, named for their scarlet tunics.

clue.text: Keen to delay unfinished glassware

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is never reached

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief

explanation.surface: Someone eager to hold back incomplete tableware.
explanation.walkthrough: Keen looks like the adjective eager; it is the verb for lamenting aloud at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal is fine, heavy glass, and the word also covers glassware made from it, such as decanters.

clue.text: Forecaster succeeded by cutting Italian article

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within the article

explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded by' looks like a link phrase, but the two words separate: one gives S, the other goes into IL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world, so someone who foretells events.

clue.text: Abhors boxes on river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone hates the boxes floating down a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes on river' puts the river first: in an across answer, 'on' means coming after.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate something is to detest or curse it, so it shares the sense of abhors.

clue.text: Model former beheaded knight

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the head, the opening letter

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a Knight Templar of the medieval crusading order

explanation.surface: A fashion model was once a knight who lost his head.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a perfect example worth copying, so a model in the sense of an ideal.

clue.text: Freakish dry season besets island for ages

parts.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.definitionFit: Donkey's years is a British idiom for a very long time, the same as ages.

clue.text: Show big wheel's fit to leave ground

parts.note: to air views is to show them
a worthy is a local dignitary, a big wheel

explanation.surface: A fairground Ferris wheel passes its safety check before the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Big wheel suggests a fairground ride; here it means an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: An airworthy aircraft is certified safe to fly, so fit to take off from the runway.

clue.text: Proud chief in Oriental sea

indicators.note: in places the chief inside the name of the sea

explanation.walkthrough: Proud has its technical sense of standing out from a surface, as a nail can stand proud.

clue.text: Himalayan legend still current?

clue.text: Heard silly old men are in possession of no man's land

clue.text: King taking a steer perhaps with queen's boatman

clue.text: Spirit in W African country good for a start

indicators.note: in places the spirit inside the country's name

explanation.surface: A drink in West Africa is fine for a start.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginning and start both name the point at which something commences.

Eli, the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

clue.text: Graphic images the norm in first of Chinese literature

clue.text: Ace actor Herbert fills lead, showing poise

clue.text: Secret police once cut period of inactivity

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so the final letter goes

clue.text: Ring theatre about a musical show
